title: Being non-technological and making a living without it
summary: Rowe jokes about the difficult Zoom; Sportiello says he has made a living playing live since age 16 without needing technology.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: The people that are watching this later on won’t know that it took me fifteen minutes to make this Zoom happen today. I’m wondering if both of us weren’t sort of born in the wrong era.

Well you know we just kept doing things, up to now, and we made a living, that did not require all this equipment, you know? You know I just made a living, traveling, and going in front of an audience and play the piano since I was 16 years old. I’m 46 now. I repeat myself. Thirty years. So I think unless you are very passionate about technology then if you don’t need it you don’t need it. I still have friends that they don’t have a cell phone because they don’t need it. They do a business, a family-run business and they don’t need a cell phone. They just have a landline phone. They barely know how to open a computer. And just because now they are imposing that you do some business with emails, you know, so that the age of seventy some years old they had to learn how to do emails. Otherwise they would have been perfectly happy still writing letters you know.
